label: Nationality discrimination in access to employment
definition: The law governing access to the labour market does not give EU workers equal treatment with nationals, for example by treating them as any other foreigner or reserving private sector posts for nationals.
exclusion_notes: Work permit, quota and residence requirements belong to RI-FMW-002; restrictions on public sector posts belong to RI-FMW-003; nationality conditions in social security laws belong to RI-FMW-009.
notes: Largest group: the same recommendation is repeated each year from 2020 to 2025. Private sector reservations are placed here rather than in RI-FMW-003; the analyst may prefer a separate issue.

label: Work permits, quotas and residence conditions applied to EU workers
definition: EU workers and their family members are subject to work permits, annual quotas, residence permits or unspecified conditions (for example for seasonal work) that must be lifted or settled by accession.
exclusion_notes: The general principle of non-discrimination and overall alignment of labour market access law belong to RI-FMW-001; posted workers' social security belongs to RI-FMW-008.
notes: Several items are the country's own description (reported view) in the screening report. MEC-02 rests on one item on seasonal work.

label: Public sector posts closed to EU citizens beyond the public authority exception
definition: EU citizens are barred from public sector posts other than a short list of exemptions, rather than only from posts involving the exercise of public authority and safeguarding the general interests of the State.
exclusion_notes: Posts reserved for nationals in private companies belong to RI-FMW-001.
notes: Repeated annual finding; the screening report adds the test of case law of the Court of Justice.

label: Legal and organisational framework for joining EURES
definition: The country has not set up the legal and organisational arrangements needed to join the European network of employment services, such as a system for appointing EURES members and partners and access for private employment agencies.
exclusion_notes: Staff training and IT capacity of the employment service belong to RI-FMW-005; the European Labour Authority belongs to RI-FMW-006.
notes: Annual reports 2020 to 2025 report no preparatory steps, while the 2025 screening report rates EURES preparation as good; this tension should be checked at classification. Items on private employment agency access also carry TECH-INTEROP.

label: Employment service capacity for EURES and labour mobility
definition: The public employment service lacks trained staff or adequate IT and data systems to take part in EU labour mobility networks and vacancy exchange.
exclusion_notes: Legal designation of EURES members and partners belongs to RI-FMW-004; electronic exchange of social security data belongs to RI-FMW-010.
notes: Several 2025 screening items are positive findings (IT in place, capacity satisfactory); the open points are training updates after staff turnover and ESCO mapping. The technology agent may draft a related TEC issue on connection to EU systems.

label: Alignment with the European Labour Authority regulation
definition: National law is not aligned with the regulation establishing the European Labour Authority, including the arrangements for cooperating with it.
exclusion_notes: EURES participation belongs to RI-FMW-004; bodies supporting mobile workers' rights belong to RI-FMW-007.
notes: Small evidence base: two findings from one source, plus mentions in the composite employment service recommendation. Candidate for merging with RI-FMW-004 or RI-FMW-007.

label: Information and support for mobile workers on their rights
definition: There is no designated body supporting EU mobile workers in their rights and the system for informing them of their rights is weak.
exclusion_notes: The substance of the rights themselves belongs to RI-FMW-001 to RI-FMW-003.
notes: Small evidence base: three items from one source (2025 screening report), two of which split one sentence. Kept separate because it is a distinct acquis obligation another country could plausibly face.

label: Gaps in bilateral social security and healthcare agreements
definition: Bilateral social security coordination and healthcare agreements do not yet cover all EU Member States or all branches, so workers moving before accession lack coordinated protection.
exclusion_notes: Alignment of national social security law with the coordination regulations belongs to RI-FMW-009; the European Health Insurance Card belongs to RI-FMW-011.
notes: Repeated annual recommendation. The screening report credits this experience as giving a good level of preparation. MEC-01 fits loosely; see the mechanism proposal on missing agreements.

label: National social security law not aligned with the coordination regulations
definition: National pension, health and other social security laws are only partly aligned with the EU coordination regulations, for example through citizenship conditions, and the administrative measures for applying them at accession are not identified or in place.
exclusion_notes: Bilateral agreements belong to RI-FMW-008; electronic exchange of social security information belongs to RI-FMW-010.

label: Readiness for electronic exchange of social security information
definition: The institutions lack the IT and human capacity to exchange social security information electronically with Member States (the EESSI system) and to use electronic health insurance data.
exclusion_notes: Legal alignment of social security law belongs to RI-FMW-009; the healthcare access rights of EHIC holders belong to RI-FMW-011.
notes: Chapter 2 issue that materially concerns the technology theme. The technology agent drafts TEC issues separately; the analyst should decide at G4 whether this issue stays under FMW, moves to TEC, or is linked to a TEC issue.

label: Access to healthcare for EU citizens through the European Health Insurance Card
definition: EU citizens can use the European Health Insurance Card or access medical services only where a bilateral arrangement exists, so access is not yet available to citizens of all Member States.
exclusion_notes: Electronic use of EHIC data belongs to RI-FMW-010; general bilateral social security agreements belong to RI-FMW-008.
notes: Overlaps with RI-FMW-008, since access depends on bilateral agreements; candidate for merging. The 2025 screening report rates EHIC technical alignment as satisfactory.

label: Supplementary pension rights of mobile workers
definition: National law is not aligned with the EU directives on supplementary pension rights, such as the acquisition and preservation of rights for workers who move between Member States.
exclusion_notes: Statutory social security pensions belong to RI-FMW-009.
notes: Single source (2025 screening report). Equal treatment in voluntary funds is already provided, entering into force at accession.

label: Weak corruption prevention in the administration of worker mobility
definition: The bodies administering free movement of workers, notably the employment service, lack a specific integrity policy, internal controls and audit capacity to prevent corruption.
exclusion_notes: General anti-corruption policy outside free movement of workers belongs to Chapter 23 and is out of scope.
notes: Included because the Commission ties these measures specifically to Chapter 2 (run record boundary). Two generic statements on ministry capacity placed in the anti-corruption section are mapped here with a note.
